bounds.domain: Two release identities in one organization, two caller organizations, two provider identities, one global idempotency key, and presence of unkeyed receipts per release. Draft content validation is a premise for marking READY. Historical data may contain one receipt on a cancelled release.
bounds.persistence: The tenant-scoped release lock and its cancellation update serialize local submission. The primary transaction records the receipt and transitions READY to submitted together. Failed transactions leave both unchanged. The existing unique key resolves competing keyed inserts. Replay requires the exact release, organization and provider and keeps the original data.
bounds.conformance: The maintained service and repository run against real PGlite using the existing press-release migration. Concurrent cancellation and submission retain one consistent database outcome. Concurrent exact submissions share one receipt, wrong identities fail, a rejected transition rolls back the insert, and historical cancelled receipts cannot acknowledge a replay.
bounds.gaps: Local state through the first submitted phase. Subsequent distribution completion, aggregation of multiple attempts, provider and payment effects, arbitrary key and receipt counts, independent native database sessions and external content delivery are outside this proof. Unkeyed receipts are projected to presence; unkeyed calls have no replay guarantee.

assumptions: Tenant, release and provider identities are immutable. Cancellation and the submission transaction serialize on the same release row. No fairness is assumed.

An exact submission and cancellation are available for the READY release, with no competing key owner. Their successful database transactions are weakly fair while continuously enabled. A rollback alone does not resolve the release.
No fairness is assumed. Available operations can wait forever or continually roll back.
